# 70_publish_comment.sh - Post a pipeline status comment to Jira

<!-- BEGIN pipeline-callers: generated by tools/automation_doc_links.py, do not edit by hand -->
:::{attention} Usually run by a Bitbucket pipeline

## Description

Posts a comment to the Jira issue of this repository, using [jira_add_comment.py](#help-jira_add_comment). The pipelines call it when they start and when they finish. The ticket is taken from `$jiraticket`, then `config.yml`, then looked up from an openICPSR directory; when none is found, nothing is posted. Failures to post never stop the pipeline.

## Usage

```bash
./automations/70_publish_comment.sh [pipeline-name] [status] [extra-message]
./automations/70_publish_comment.sh --config [pipeline-name] [extra-message]
```

- `pipeline-name` - Name of the Bitbucket pipeline. No built-in Bitbucket variable provides it, so the pipeline passes it.
- `status` - `started` or `completed` (default: `completed`). Other values are used as given.
- `extra-message` - Appended to the comment, for example the "Software detected: ..." line from [26_update_jira_software.sh](#help-26_update_jira_software).
- `--config` - Post the uncommitted `git diff -- config.yml` instead of a status message. Nothing is posted when there is no diff.

The status comment links to the Bitbucket build, using `BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE`, `BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG` and `BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER`.

### Environment Variables

- `jiraticket`, `JIRA_USERNAME`, `JIRA_API_KEY`
